Vocally and physically, it’s a well-balanced quartet: Russell the inscrutable, breathy waif, Essiedu with a dancer’s grace and rascally charm, Austin rueful and sympathetic, and Holdbrook-Smith wielding a velvety basso.
But it’s a conceptual imposition, which paradoxically keeps intellectual engagement secondary, at best.
While the central courtship is at times charmingly depicted, the writing proves so schematic and artificial that the play not only takes place in a lab but feels like it was written in one as well.
The Effect has given us a huge gymnasium into which we are invited to play, engage, risk, contemplate, judge, experiment, and be our wild selves.
Director Jamie Lloyd's production, first mounted last year in London, sizzles with sensational performances by an unlikely couple...

cn.t: Prebble's provocative drama about love and brain chemistry receives a stark, riveting production with galvanizing performances, though some find Lloyd's minimalist staging overly schematic and the experimental approach distracting.
